question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}y({x}^{2}+1),\, & -1\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $\text{E}[X]=0$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{2}{3},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{3}{4}y({x}^{2}+1))\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{4}+{x}^{2})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot {[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{-1}^{1}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{16}{15}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}-{(0)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}(\frac{3}{4}y({x}^{2}+1))\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x]}_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$ The joint support of $X$ and $Y$ is given by the rectangle

$$
S=[-1,1]\times [0,1].
$$

Moreover, we can write

$$
f(x,y)=g(x)\cdot h(y),
$$

where $g(x)=\frac{3}{8}({x}^{2}+1)$ and $h(y)=2y.$

Hence, $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and consequently $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{18}\end{aligned}].
$$
